To put it another way:  sure, I'm not a computer expert. But I'm not a novice.  And the Stan installation keeps defeating me.  If I'm defeated, I'm guessing that other potential users are getting defeated too.  And they might just be giving up, they're not necessarily sending messages to the help list like I am!

A

---

Ummm, more problems.  I tried to follow the instructions:

---

One way you can achieve this is to execute this from within R:

if (!file.exists("~/.R/Makevars")) {
  cat('CXX=g++ -arch x86_64 -ftemplate-depth-256 -stdlib=libstdc++
       CXXFLAGS="-mtune=native  -O3 -Wall -pedantic -Wconversion" ', 
       file="~/.R/Makevars");
} else {
   file.show("~/.R/Makevars");
}

If the Makevars file already exists, its content will be displayed and you can decide whether to run the cat part of the above command and destroy the existing Makevars file.

> Hi all. I'm struggling to install the new Rstan (see some details below).

I'm really sorry you're frustrated. I hate installing
software myself. It's why I keep trying to cut down on the
dependencies so we don't have so many moving parts. But it
appears to be pretty much impossible with the way R is set up,
with ever changing compilers and interfaces like Rcpp and
build environments that get pulled out from under us when users install
other packages. And this doesn't even get into the complexity of
RStudio.

> I wonder if we could have some more
> automated instructions, maybe a makefile or whatever it is called? Looking at the help file, it seems pretty
> algorithmic (if the computer has X installed, do Y, if it's a mac, do this, if it's a PC, do that, it if's later than

Let me turn this around. Either it's not so algorithmic
or you didn't follow the instructions!

> As is, I'd say that of the 5 or so times I've
> installed Stan,

That's RStan --- command-line Stan is much much easier to
install because it doesn't have as many dependencies. This
isn't a dig at RStan --- it's caused by the fact that R is just
a way more complex environment. It's impossible to pin down the
moving pieces on a user's system from the outside.

> it's worked the first time about half the time, other times I need to get help. So, even though doing
> an automated install would be a pain in the ass, maybe it would not be so bad, as it would formalize all the choices in
> the install in one programmed place. Then we can have a document for the experts explaining what got done.

If you can hire the staff to do it or convince the volunteers
we have to do it in their spare time rather than doing something
else, by all means! I believe the only developer we have with even
remotely enough experience to do this for RStan is Ben.

And remember, it's not a one-time job. Every time Rcpp, RStudio,
the Mac OS, the compilers, etc. change, it has to be redone. We just
don't have the staff to do this.

> To put it another way: sure, I'm not a computer expert. But I'm not a novice. And the Stan installation keeps
> defeating me. If I'm defeated, I'm guessing that other potential users are getting defeated too. And they might just
> be giving up, they're not necessarily sending messages to the help list like I am!

I'm very worried that you're right.

- Bob

By the way, have you updated to the newest xcode?  If not, you should ignore that part of modifying ~/.R/Makevars file.

I take it the newest xcode uses libc++ by default, which is why it is necessary for ~/.R/Makevars to override that. If so, then we can probably eliminate that once the C++11 branch is merged because then Stan would probably compile with libc++ even if -std=c++11 was not specified.

Ben
